instructions: Grate a quarter of the cucumber into a clean kitchen towel or a sieve and squeeze out as much water as you can, or the tzatziki will be runny. That should be about 1/3 cup.

In a bowl, stir together the grated cucumber, 3/4 cup yogurt, 1/2 of the garlic clove, grated, 2 tsp lemon juice, 2 tsp olive oil, 2 tsp chopped dill and 1/4 tsp salt. Set it in the fridge while you slice.
Slice the rest of the cucumber thinly. Slice the tomatoes and the onion thinly, and crumble the feta.
Warm the pitas, 2 at a time, wrapped in a damp paper towel in the microwave for 10 to 15 seconds, until soft.
Fill each pita with cucumber, tomato and onion. Spoon in the tzatziki, then sprinkle with the feta and 1/2 tsp of the oregano.
Serve right away with any extra tzatziki on the side. If you're packing them, keep the tzatziki and the vegetables in separate containers for up to 2 days and fill the pitas just before you eat.
method_notes: Fork in the Kitchen's veggie pitas are the lead: warmed pita, sliced tomato, cucumber and onion, tzatziki, oregano and feta. Its tzatziki is a link to another page, so the tzatziki here follows Cup of Yum (Greek yogurt, grated cucumber, garlic, lemon, olive oil, dill) scaled to 4 pitas. Both agree on squeezing the cucumber dry and filling the pita just before eating; Fork in the Kitchen uses raw onion since its 2022 update, and so does this version.
